page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra processor family using Neoverse-N1 cores. Running under the QEMU hypervisor, this instance features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU resources are shared rather than dedicated. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core, and includes 80 GB of local SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the cax21 delivers entry-level to moderate performance. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieves average tier results with a single-core score of 1805.19 and a multi-core score of 7235.85. However, memory subsystem performance is constrained, with Passmark memory scores and uncached large-block read/write bandwidths falling into the weak and poor categories. Real-world application benchmarks show average performance for database operations and single-threaded gzip compression, but weak results in software compilation, text processing, and static web serving throughput. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are poor, registering 168.92 tokens per second for prompt processing and 12.5 tokens per second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cax21 offers a resource-dense hardware profile suitable for budget-conscious deployments where dedicated CPU performance is not a strict requirement. The shared CPU allocation and ARM architecture lower the entry barrier for multi-core environments. This server is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, development and testing environments, simple database operations, and utility scripting that can leverage ARM64 architecture without demanding high memory bandwidth or sustained peak CPU performance.
